item.title: Judge accuses DOJ of 'weaponization,' tosses case against ex-FBI officials
item.description:
A federal judge tossed criminal charges against two former FBI officials accused of lying to Congress about the Hunter Biden investigation Monday, delivering a blistering rebuke of the prosecution and accusing the Trump administration's Justice Department of weaponizing the justice system. U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui dismissed the criminal complaint against former FBI officials Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides from the bench, sharply criticizing the government's handling of the prosecution. "What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization," Faruqui said, describing the case as a "rush job" directed by President Donald Trump and FBI Director Kash Patel. item.title: US to drop South Africa, Rwanda from duty-free trade initiative
item.description:
The News US President Donald Trump plans to remove South Africa and Rwanda from African Growth and Opportunity Act eligibility next year, stripping both countries of duty-free access to the US market under Washington’s flagship Africa trade program. Trump formally notified Congress and both governments of his decision, the Office of the US Trade Representative said Monday, after an annual review determined Pretoria and Kigali have been engaging in “concerning and pervasive” practices inconsistent with AGOA’s eligibility criteria. These include “barriers that undermine American trade and investment” and practices that “pose a threat to US national security and foreign policy interests in the region,” US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said. item.title: Karl Bushby embraces his mother as he completes his 28-year walk around world
item.description:
“They say it takes a village. In this case, it took a world.” After 28 years and some 50,000 kilometres, British explorer and adventurer Karl Bushby has returned to his hometown of Hull, completing an extraordinary life journey across four continents that illustrates not only the limits of human endurance, but also the intricate relationship between individual determination, geopolitical constraints and a world of humanity. Speaking to France 24's François Picard shortly after his emotional homecoming, Bushby reflects on an undertaking that resembles a modern-day Odyssey, although the defining obstacles were often more geopolitical than mythological.

item.title: Student protests resume in France as pupils return to school
item.description:
Jennie Shin is pleased to welcome Éric Fassin, Sociologist and Professor at Université Paris 8. “In a democracy, elections are very important, but it’s not the end of democracy. It’s the beginning,” explains Fassin. He interprets France’s student protest movement growing into a challenge to socioeconomic policy and what he describes as an “illiberal turn” in government. Connecting the treatment of working-class, racialized youth with wider restrictions on dissent, he argues that racism and democratic participation are central to understanding the unrest. His analysis also challenges the attribution of responsibility to the left, placing the government’s response within a broader debate over the normalization of oppressive measures and the far right.

Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24, The Guardian

item.title: What Florida jet audio and flight data tells us about its final moments
item.description:
A chilling recording of the final moments aboard a Learjet 60 that crashed in Florida, killing all nine people aboard, captured a man believed to be the pilot reciting the Lord’s Prayer. The audio, recorded during the plane’s final communications with air traffic control , captures the man saying, “hallowed be Thy name.” His identity has not been officially confirmed. The crash occurred Sunday near West Palm Beach as the jet traveled from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas. The co-pilot has been identified by her family as 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras , but authorities have not yet publicly identified the other victims. The crew reported worsening conditions at approximately 35,000 feet. item.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
item.description:
Chains in seven countries say cooling unit temperatures rose overnight in incident similar to hack of French shops Who is hacking Europe’s supermarket fridges and freezers, and why? Supermarket chains in at least seven European countries have said the temperatures of refrigerators and freezers in some of their shops soared overnight to as high as 50C (122F), echoing a cyber-attack last month that caused millions of euros of damage in France. Retailers in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden reported problems with their refrigeration systems on Monday, and several companies confirmed they had been hacked. item.title: Washington state resident dies from bird flu following exposure to infected cattle
item.description:
Individual, who also had underlying conditions, was hospitalized after being exposed to avian influenza A Washington state resident has died after being hospitalized with “severe illness” after contracting bird flu, local health officials said on Sunday. The individual was exposed to avian influenza, also known as bird flu, at a dairy with infected cattle in Yakima county, according to a news release . The person was subsequently hospitalized with severe illness and died on Sunday. Health officials said that the individual, whose identity had not been released, had underlying health conditions.
